lines.say: What if the witch pouring
this poison is secretly sorry?
This is Circe Invidiosa,
painted by John William Waterhouse in 1892.
Everyone knows Circe from Ovid
as the jealous witch who made a monster.
Glaucus loved Scylla instead of her,
so she poisoned Scylla's pool.
And the picture seems to agree.
Green poison pours from her bowl,
and dark shapes already swirl below.
But look at her face.
It is grave, not gleeful.
According to the critic Chris Woods,
Waterhouse did not paint his Circe as wholly evil.
Here she becomes a tragic figure
who cannot help what she is doing.
And she rather regrets it.
She isn't a gloating monster.
She's a woman watching her own jealousy work.
So is she a cruel witch,
or a woman who cannot stop herself?
